code: phi <- (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2 barth <- function(x, y, z) {   x2 <- x^2; y2 <- y^2; z2 <- z^2   v <- 3 * (phi^2 * x2 - y2) * (phi^2 * y2 - z2) * (phi^2 * z2 - x2) -     (1 + 2 * phi) * (x2 + y2 + z2 - 1)^2   ifelse(x2 + y2 + z2 > 3.1, NA, v) } ggplot() +   geom_isofunction_3d(fun = barth, levels = 0, n = 48, fill = PAL[["blue"]]) +   cube(1.8) + coord_3d() clebsch <- function(x, y, z) {   81 * (x^3 + y^3 + z^3) - 189 * (x^2 * (y + z) + y^2 * (z + x) + z^2 * (x + y)) +     54 * x * y * z + 126 * (x * y + y * z + z * x) - 9 * (x^2 + y^2 + z^2) -     9 * (x + y + z) + 1 } ggplot() +   geom_isofunction_3d(fun = clebsch, levels = 0, n = 40, fill = PAL[["orange"]]) +   cube(1) + coord_3d()

Hirota’s direct method (Hirota 2004) writes solitons u=2(log⁡τ)xxu = 2 (\log \tau)_{xx}. ηi=kix+liy−ωit\eta_i = k_i x + l_i y - \omega_i t ωi=(ki4+3li2)/ki\omega_i = (k_i^4 + 3 l_i^2) / k_i, function τ=1+eη1\tau = 1 + e^{\eta_1} gives one line soliton, straight crest height k12/2k_1^2 / 2, τ=1+eη1+eη2+A12eη1+η2,A12=l2l2−1for k1=k2=1,l1=−l2=l,\tau = 1 + e^{\eta_1} + e^{\eta_2} + A_{12}\, e^{\eta_1 + \eta_2}, \qquad A_{12} = \frac{l^2}{l^2 - 1} \quad \text{} k_1 = k_2 = 1,\ l_1 = -l_2 = l, gives two line solitons cross X. solution regular l>1l > 1. l=1.2l = 1.2 crests travel xx direction speed ω1/k1=5.32\omega_1 / k_1 = 5.32, segment meet shifted forward stands higher either crest alone.
code: l <- 1.2 kp_omega <- 1 + 3 * l^2 kp <- function(x, y, t) {   e1 <- exp(x + l * y - kp_omega * t)   e2 <- exp(x - l * y - kp_omega * t)   a12 <- l^2 / (l^2 - 1)   tau <- 1 + e1 + e2 + a12 * e1 * e2   tau_x <- e1 + e2 + 2 * a12 * e1 * e2   tau_xx <- e1 + e2 + 4 * a12 * e1 * e2   2 * (tau_xx * tau - tau_x^2) / tau^2 } crossing <- solution_frames(kp, times = seq(-2.2, 2.2, length.out = 40),                             range = c(-10, 10), n = 61) p <- ggplot(crossing, aes(x, y, z = u, fill = after_stat(z_mean))) +   geom_surface_3d(colour = NA) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey85", high = PAL[["blue"]]) +   coord_3d(azimuth = -50, elevation = 35) +   labs(z = "u") knitr::include_graphics(animate(p))

Two kinks combine closed form (Hirota 2004): u=4arctan⁡eη1+eη21+a12eη1+η2,a12=(p1−p2)2+(q1−q2)2−(ω1−ω2)2(p1+p2)2+(q1+q2)2−(ω1+ω2)2.u = 4 \arctan \frac{e^{\eta_1} + e^{\eta_2}}{1 + a_{12}\, e^{\eta_1 + \eta_2}}, \qquad a_{12} = \frac{(p_1 - p_2)^2 + (q_1 - q_2)^2 - (\omega_1 - \omega_2)^2}{(p_1 + p_2)^2 + (q_1 + q_2)^2 - (\omega_1 + \omega_2)^2}. frames use one front along yy axis moving +x+x one along xx axis moving −y-y, speed 0.6. surface stands 2π2\pi two opposite quadrants exactly one η1\eta_1, η2\eta_2 positive lies near 0 two; corner fronts cross moves along diagonal.
code: sine_gordon <- function(x, y, t) {   p <- 1.25   w <- sqrt(p^2 - 1)   e1 <- exp(p * x - w * t)   e2 <- exp(p * y + w * t)   a12 <- (2 * p^2 - 4 * w^2) / (2 * p^2)   4 * atan((e1 + e2) / (1 + a12 * e1 * e2)) } kinks <- solution_frames(sine_gordon, times = seq(-8, 8, length.out = 33),                          range = c(-8, 8), n = 51) p <- ggplot(kinks, aes(x, y, z = u, fill = after_stat(z_mean))) +   geom_surface_3d(colour = NA) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey85", high = PAL[["purple"]]) +   coord_3d(azimuth = -50, elevation = 35) +   labs(z = "u") knitr::include_graphics(animate(p))
